relevance.rationale: Argues that a full theoretical account of the double-slit experiment requires the JOINT position-and-time distribution of detection (whose position marginal is the familiar fringe pattern), notes there is no consensus quantum time observable, and computes the joint distribution within Bohmian mechanics for a Gaussian packet through a double slit and for a slit shut during flight; it concludes that sufficient longitudinal spread is needed for the temporal aspect to be non-classical, and illustrates against a published helium-atom joint position-time dataset. The corpus does have a double-slit cluster (q-double-slit, double-slit-analytical, double-slit-massive-pattern, double-slit-two-modes), so the subject overlaps genuinely. But those blocks are intensity-envelope simulators — a q-deformed fringe prediction validated against an electron dataset (bach2013, the only citation in the cluster) — with no trajectory ontology, no arrival-time observable, and no joint distribution anywhere. The paper's result is a statement about a time observable in a framework the corpus does not have, so there is no place here that wants it. Scope-(a): this document, as read, supplies nothing this folio can consume; it is not a claim that arrival-time structure is irrelevant to a q-deformed interference model.

proposedActions.rationale: Read and judged to need nothing. If the folio ever states a q-deformed prediction for detection TIME rather than position, this becomes a live comparison; today it has no such statement.
